author: Keel (brief 010, 2026-10-15)
rule: Every event the city simulation runs: what it needs, what it charges, what it changes and who sees it (GDD §11: events carry conditions, effects, witnesses). Anything not in this file or in people.rules.json is rejected (§01: unknown = reject). Scales, temperaments, needs, ties, the Talker test, knowledge and the reference approach prices are read from people.rules.json through p: refs and condition kinds, never restated here. Every number lives once in `values`, tagged as the GDD tags it: [B] built and proven in the top-down test, [S] starting value to tune by playtest, [L] later; a value or rule the GDD does not decide carries proposed: true and a reason, for Sky. Conditions are keyed by `k`, effects by `do`, always the first key, so the C# engine reads them as tagged unions. Outcomes are tried in order and the first whose conditions all hold applies; the last has none, so every event resolves to exactly one outcome. `also` entries apply after the outcome, in order.

reads: scales: min, max and named steps; every move clamps to them
temperaments: respondsTo, refuses and reportsApproach decide an approach's fit; start values
approaches: requires, usd, timeS and trail are the base price line of each Turn event
needs.list: metBy (which approach acts on a need), requires (what a replacement need may need)
knowledge: needsKnown positions (K9), identity face only, learnedBy witnessed or told
tiers: only the simulated carry memory and can be questioned (Sky Q5)

tags.B: built: proven in the top-down test (~/Projects/the-suborned/testbed/reference/suborned-world-sim.cjs) or stated [B] in the GDD
tags.S: spec: a starting value the GDD states [S], tuned by playtest

units.s: integer seconds; the engine steps at 10 Hz (§11), so 1 s = 10 ticks
units.standing: district standing, integer: above 0 Hero, below 0 Menace
units.orders: orders of the same approach to the same person
units.hops: ties crossed by one piece of news
units.per-mille: integer weight scale for seeded draws

watch-s.src: Sky 2026-10-15 (Motive's balance, briefs/011/motive-balance.md): Watch 20 s; §04 Pay requires routine known (Watch); the top-down test's watchCafe was 52 s [B]
watch-s.reason: Motive balance (brief 011, Suture E-8, T2): at 52 s the informed route A calls at 2:42 and loud (3:38) beats it. At 20 s the call is at 2:10, inside the 2:13-2:47 sweep gap, and route A finishes at 3:33, 5 s before the best loud. Watch keeps its place in the chain (Watch, then Listen, then Help) and Sky's Pay lesson stays on the main path: after Watch the Pay card shows '?' and $90,000 worst case. standing-start.src: Sky 2026-10-16 ('Hero is kinda the default, if you're not seen then everyone assumes you're good (it's that kinda world)'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rule 1 (approved by Sky, 'sure', 2026-10-16); was 0
standing-start.reason: Motive: every district starts leaning Hero, one step short of the Hero band, so one known kindness earns the band. Starting at +3 would put the Handover in Hero prices from the first second and change its tested costs; at +2 every in-mission price stays neutral.

standing-step.src: §04 standing: witnessed acts only; §05 witness moves standing
standing-step.reason: one step per witnessed incident, as Trail counts one point per incident: one incident counts once.

hero-at.src: §04 standing table (turning, crowds, fights, street change at each end)
hero-at.reason: the Hero and Menace columns need a threshold. Three witnessed incidents one way make a district Hero (or Menace at −3): a mission or two of deliberate play, so the player sees it coming and chooses it.

word-standing-step.src: Sky 2026-10-16 ('if you help in a good way then can move to hero'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rules 2 and 3
word-standing-step.reason: Motive: between missions each person the cell helped tells their ties a stranger helped them (+1), and each person it pressured or knocked out tells of the harm (−1): one step per person, not per tie, so a large family is no lever.

word-standing-cap.src: Sky 2026-10-16 ('if you help in a good way then can move to hero'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rules 2 and 3
word-standing-cap.reason: Motive: the word moves a district at most 2 steps either way in one mission, so turning a crowd of kind strangers cannot buy the Hero band outright and a bad mission's word cannot sink a district alone; seen and found acts stay uncapped.

standing-drift.src: Sky 2026-10-16 (approved Motive's 'the benefit of the doubt'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rule 5
standing-drift.reason: Motive: what the city stops seeing, it forgives. A district where nothing moved Standing this mission moves 1 step back toward standing-start, from either side, never past it: unkept Hero fades back to +2 as Menace does, so Hero is kept by doing good and a Menace cell is not stuck.

fight-standing-step.src: Sky 2026-10-16 (via Aster: 'it should be per fight, and depends who you're fighting - a rival gang that has menace level authority is a +1'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md, a public fight, rule 3
fight-standing-step.reason: Motive: the public judges a fight by its enemy, once per fight: one step, toward Menace for a fight with authority or for firing first on rivals nobody fears, toward Hero for driving off a crew the district fears.

When full the oldest goes: an old sighting is forgotten, which is the GDD's 'sightings go stale' (§05 counters) made a rule. Fixed size suits the engine's integer arrays.

word-quiet-loyalty.src: §01 pillar subvert people: does knowing more make a person quieter?; Motive's review #10 (briefs/010/motive-rulebook-review.md)
word-quiet-loyalty.reason: a person who owes the cell (obliged or more) keeps what they saw to themselves; one Help, which needs a Listen, is enough; at 2 a helped Inez would lie to investigators and still tell her family the Fixer's face. Obliged is also the line for reporting and selling.

fight-ambush-m.reason: the ambush springs when the Enforcer brings Vale within 20 m of the getaway car: close enough that the car is the bait, far enough that the Enforcer can't just step in.

fight-hold-m.src: Sky 2026-10-18, brief 018 the getaway (Motive), option 3: "get my team into the car, and get away"; was 25 m (§07 final fight [S]: always)
fight-hold-m.reason: a hostile within 8 m reaches a door in 5 s at the rivals' 1.6 m/s, about pistol point blank (5 m) plus a car's width. The ambush and police stops (12–19 m) stand outside it, so the car is held by those who come for it, not by the fight around it.

fight-block-m.src: Sky 2026-10-18, brief 018 the getaway (Motive), option 3: "get my team into the car, and get away"
fight-block-m.reason: the stretch a car needs to pull out of a kerb bay and reach speed (about 4 s at 3.5 m/s²); a body in it is in the car's way. The exit lane is this much of the getaway route's carriageway ahead of the car (site getaway.exit).

fight-block-near-m.reason: beyond fight-hold-m (8 m) and point-blank (5 m): the blocker holds the lane, not the door, and the cell's cover works against it. Also the open post: the lane centreline this far from its start when no cover stands in the ring

fight-block-far-m.reason: inside pistol-eff-m (15 m) by 2 m: the cell at the car and the blocker are in each other's effective reach, so the fight starts and Go is never a standoff

fight-blockers.src: Sky 2026-10-18, brief 018 the getaway (Motive), option 3: "get my team into the car, and get away"
fight-blockers.reason: one hostile per fight goes for the road. It doesn't pass on, so the car is freed by downing one, not all.

investigators-base.src: §05 investigators [S][L]: count rises with A and T
investigators-base.reason: one investigator works any open Trail; the count is what the debrief reads, so it says how hard the city looks.

investigators-per-alert.src: §05 investigators: count rises with A and T
investigators-per-alert.reason: +1 investigator for each Alert level the mission reached: a lockdown sends four.

investigator-hops.src: §05 investigators: ~60–90 s per hop; useful answer → go there, question again
investigator-hops.reason: each investigator follows two leads before the next mission (a hop is one person questioned, §05's 60–90 s, and the debrief reads the result). Two hops are one step up the chain and one more: the Talker who saw the Fixer, then whoever stood where that Talker points.

run-alert.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md; §05 Alert 1 [S]: found fault, once per incident
run-alert.reason: a runner seen by the guard, the patrol, a live camera or the response unit is a found fault: Alert rises to at least 1, once per run order.

board-s.src: Sky 2026-10-18, brief 018 the getaway (Motive), option 3: "get my team into the car, and get away"
board-s.reason: getting in or out of a car beside it; carrying, carry-s more, the carried first (putting a body in mirrors lifting it)

carry-s.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md §2.4, §2.10: carry a downed operative
carry-s.reason: lifting a downed operative takes 3 s; then the carrier walks only and doesn't fire (§06 downed: carry or captured).

gunfire-trail.src: Sky-approved fights, Motive addendum 2026-10-15 (briefs/011/motive-fights.md, Addendum) Q1; §02 Trail: gunfire is a traceable act
gunfire-trail.reason: a shooting is a case: the first shot at each target costs +2 T, hit or miss (shots heard on a civic square open a file); the final fight stays untraced. Loud goes to 9 T, above Pressure (8).

draw-incident-s.src: Sky-approved fights, Motive addendum 2026-10-15 (briefs/011/motive-fights.md, Addendum) Q1: drawn weapons at one place are one incident
draw-incident-s.reason: Keel: the cell drawing on one order, or one beat apart (c003: the Scout and the Fixer 0.9 s apart), is one sight; a second draw 5 s or more later, or beyond witness range of the first, is a new act. Place is the witness range (witness-range-m).

lover-stay-s.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door §1.4; §07 route A: stays 60 s
lover-stay-s.reason: one value for every lover in every mission; the mission reads it, never restates it.

summon-walk-max-s.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door §1.4
summon-walk-max-s.reason: keeps a summons local, about one block (≤ 126 m at 1.4 m/s); the Handover's walk fits; bounds the absence at ≤ 4 min, so no generated mission gets an endless lure.

summon-alert-max.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door §1.4
summon-alert-max.reason: he answers through an inquiry (Alert 1) but not a search (Alert 2: security staff stay at their posts): the lure is for a quiet run.

summons-per-shift.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door §1.4
summons-per-shift.reason: he can't be missed twice; it also stops call-spam lure loops.

together-m.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door §1.2
together-m.reason: watching them together: the mission's near and approach-reach-m, 4 m.

point-blank-m.reason: can't miss at arm's length: 1000 ‰ inside 5 m.

pistol-every-ticks.reason: Syndicate-fast: a shot every 1.5 s. The [B] 6 s was a turn-length proxy from the top-down test.

pistol-eff-m.reason: the Handover's fights stand 12–19 m from the car, so a pistol fights at the edge of its effective band.

pistol-max-m.src: Sky 2026-10-20 (tuning.md §7.9: "yeah, promote both": the lab's 16 m sidearm to today); Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md (was 25 m)
pistol-max-m.reason: 1 m past the effective ring (the lab sidearm's max, lab-sidearm-max-m): the stand-off band where a shooter hits what can't answer shrinks to 15–16 m, and the kite response answers it. Was 25 m: beyond the cones' 18–22 m, you could hit what can't see you, badly.

carbine-damage.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md; §06 heavier 2–3: the Enforcer's carbine

carbine-eff-m.reason: the carbine fights inside the Handover's 12–19 m spots.

carbine-max-m.reason: as the pistol's long band, five metres on.

acc-eff.reason: effective band: exactly three hits in four (the accumulator).

acc-long.reason: long band: two in five, the first a miss.

acc-start.reason: the accumulator's start when a shooter takes a new target: a 50 %+ shot hits first.

mod-moving.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: accuracy halved while walking
mod-moving.reason: walk and shoot halves it (tuning.md §8.3: a run quarters it, a run away an eighth).

mod-running.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (build 0.2.19: fire on the move), Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §8.3
mod-running.reason: tuning.md §8.3: a run toward or across quarters the shot: firing on the run is allowed, never the best way to fight

mod-running-away.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (build 0.2.19: fire on the move), Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §8.3
mod-running-away.reason: tuning.md §8.3: running away fires at an eighth: suppression while breaking contact, not killing fire

mod-target-running.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (build 0.2.19: fire on the move), Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §8.3
mod-target-running.reason: tuning.md §8.3: a running target is a little harder to hit, past point blank only, one step that never stacks with cover (a mover has none), so running in the open is always easier to hit than standing in cover

run-away-cone-deg.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (build 0.2.19: fire on the move), Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §8.3
run-away-cone-deg.reason: tuning.md §8.3: a run step within 60° of straight away from the target is a run away; the edge counts as away

mod-cover.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: halved again against a target beside cover
mod-cover.reason: a target standing still beside cover; the cover points are Pulse's build-time data (until they land, nobody is beside cover).

mod-vale.reason: the Enforcer holding Vale fires one-handed.

mod-untrained.reason: the Scout, the Fixer, the Tech and the rivals are no trained fighters; the Enforcer, officers and the guard are.

follow-m.src: Sky on firing 2026-10-21 (brief 024: "all agents near would fire same target if not engaged"); Motive, briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §11.1
follow-m.reason: near is one ring round the driven agent: the E prompt's reach and fight-hold-m; it holds a squad that came when called and leaves out an agent posted at another door.

auto-holster-s.src: brief 030 §5 (Sky 2026-10-20: "yes, try it (gun drawn by a click or panic holsters 4 s after the fight ends; drawn with F stays until F)"); Glyph, briefs/030-contextual-act.md
auto-holster-s.reason: long enough to see the fight is over, short enough that a gun the fight made the cell draw is not left out on a calm street (a drawn weapon seen raises Alert).

draw-ticks.reason: drawing is a visible beat (1.0 s); the going-loud gate sits on it.

aim-new-ticks.reason: a shooter whose weapon is drawn fires 1.0 s after taking a new target.

react-s.reason: a hostile's surprise on first sight of the cell outside a fight.

line-lapse-s.reason: a fire order holds its aim this long when the line breaks, then lapses.

sidearm-arms.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md (Q1): the whole cell armed, one sidearm per point of Arms; the Enforcer's carbine is the cell's and uses none

health-enforcer.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md; §06 health [S][L] brought forward to the Handover

health-op.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md; §06 health: Scout, Fixer, Tech 4

health-camera.src: Sky 2026-10-21 ("players should be able to shoot anyone"), Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §9.2 gap 2
health-camera.reason: tuning.md §9.2: a camera is a target: one hit (×healthScale in the lab: one sidearm hit) and it is dark for the rest of the mission; the shot is gunfire, no hit or down Trail, no Standing

health-car.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (tuning.md §9.7: cars "shootable, as in Syndicate"); Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §10.7
health-car.reason: tuning.md §10.7: 10 pistol hits or 5 carbine hits in today; ×healthScale in the lab (100: 10 sidearm or 5 carbine hits)

car-disabled-at.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (tuning.md §9.7: cars "shootable, as in Syndicate"); Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §10.7
car-disabled-at.reason: tuning.md §10.7: at or below half its health a car is disabled: it stops where it is and can't drive, its occupants get out; ×healthScale in the lab (50)

car-burn-s.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (tuning.md §9.7: cars "shootable, as in Syndicate"); Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §10.7
car-burn-s.reason: tuning.md §10.7: at 0 a car burns for 6 s (its blast ring shows on the ground), then explodes; the same in the lab

car-blast-m.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (tuning.md §9.7: cars "shootable, as in Syndicate"); Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §10.7
car-blast-m.reason: tuning.md §10.7: one ring, 5 m from the car

car-blast-damage.src: Sky 2026-10-21 (tuning.md §9.7: cars "shootable, as in Syndicate"); Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §10.7
car-blast-damage.reason: tuning.md §10.7: to everyone inside the ring with a line to the car, the cell included (blasts don't ask whose they are), and to occupants still inside; ×healthScale in the lab (30)

response-officers.reason: the response unit as two officers, so downing it is a fight, not one 2-hit target.

hit-trail.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: the cost moves from the shot to the victim
hit-trail.reason: +2 T per person hit, once. A dropped guard still costs 4 T, as the [B] two shots did.

down-trail.reason: +2 T more when they go down.

gunfire-alert.reason: any gunfire raises Alert to at least 2, in place of +1 a shot: §05's own rule, which settles the §05/§06 conflict the alert rule recorded.

draw-seen-security-alert.reason: a drawn weapon in the cone of the guard, the patrol, a live camera or the response unit: Alert to at least 2, and that watcher engages (Syndicate's police shoot an agent with a weapon out).

draw-seen-people-alert.reason: a drawn weapon seen within 13 m by people is one witnessed incident: +1 T, Alert at least 1, and they remember the face.

loud-commit-hold-ticks.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md (Q4): the going-loud card commits with a 0.5 s hold, no pause
loud-commit-hold-ticks.reason: the host's hold; the engine reports it with the going-loud query so the card and the rule share one number.

enter-alarm-s.src: Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md (Q5): Enter takes +30 s once Alert ≥ 2
enter-alarm-s.reason: the Office staff hide Vale once the alarm is up: §05's search made physical in the one building that matters, and it keeps route A level with the fastest loud run (T2).

cover-snap-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI (Pulse) §5; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
cover-snap-cm.reason: a body is beside a cover point within 70 cm: the walk grid cell is 50 cm and the body keeps 65 cm off a solid (plan standards.walking.body.r), so a body that reached the point's cell is within 70 cm of it

cover-q-full.src: tools/cover/gen.ts RULES.qFull; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
cover-q-full.reason: a waist-high run seen across a wide arc (800 × (250 + 750 × 40/60) / 1000 = 600) is full cover: the hit modifier mod-cover (Motive, 500 per mille)

cover-q-partial.src: tools/cover/gen.ts RULES.qPartial; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
cover-q-partial.reason: below 350 an object is a post or a stump, not cover: it is not written to the file

mod-cover-partial.src: Motive's mod-cover is 500 (briefs/011/motive-fights.md §2.2); Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
mod-cover-partial.reason: partial cover (a narrow or low object) halves nothing but takes a quarter off: 750 per mille. Motive owns the number

cover-retreat-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
cover-retreat-cm.reason: an advancing hostile takes cover no more than 2 m back from its objective: it is going somewhere

cover-step-closer-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
cover-step-closer-cm.reason: a hostile in a fight steps to cover no more than 3 m nearer its target than it stands: cover is for staying alive, not for charging

cover-step-gap-s.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
cover-step-gap-s.reason: at most one step to cover each 4 s, so a body that has taken cover does not shuffle between two points

cover-leave-s.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
cover-leave-s.reason: a body leaves cover only after it has been unprotected from its target for 2 s: the target moved round it

ai-engage-lapse-s.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.2; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
ai-engage-lapse-s.reason: a body that has lost every foe from reach and sight stays stopped 1 s before it advances again, so a foe stepping behind a pier does not make it dance

ai-reacquire-s.src: Motive line-lapse-s 3 (briefs/011/motive-fights.md §2.4); Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
ai-reacquire-s.reason: a target reacquired within 3 s of losing it is shot at once: aim-new-s is waived. This is what makes police suppress

ai-stop-reach-pct.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.2; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
ai-stop-reach-pct.reason: an advancing body halts at 90% of its weapon's effective reach from its foe or objective: inside the band, not on its edge

ai-stand-overflow-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §3.3; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
ai-stand-overflow-cm.reason: a second body sent to a police stand takes the nearest free cover point within 8 m, else a slot 1.2 m beside the stand (about two body widths)

ai-seek-rival-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.3; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
ai-seek-rival-cm.reason: 8 m: a run of 5 s at the rivals' 1.6 m/s

ai-seek-police-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §2.3; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)

ai-seek-response-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §3.3; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
ai-seek-response-cm.reason: 12 m: the response unit arrives from the street, not from a post, and takes the nearest cover about the stands

ai-seek-ally-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §3.4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)

ai-seek-guard-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §3.5; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
ai-seek-guard-cm.reason: 4 m round the door: he holds it

rival-gone-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §3.1; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
rival-gone-cm.reason: a rival that broke is gone when it is within 1 m of its car

guard-return-s.src: brief 011 fight AI §3.5; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
guard-return-s.reason: he goes back to the door 10 s after the last foe left his reach

patrol-resume-s.src: brief 011 fight AI §3.6; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (Motive owns the number)
patrol-resume-s.reason: the patrol resumes its sweep 15 s after the last foe left its reach

crowd-scatter-m.src: Motive §2.7: people within 30 m of gunfire scatter; the same 30 m as patrol-break-m [B]; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4 (Motive owns the number)
crowd-scatter-m.reason: the whole block's square is within 30 m of a fight at the getaway car

crowd-startle-ticks.src: brief 011 fight AI §4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4 (Motive owns the number)
crowd-startle-ticks.reason: a person starts to run half a second after a shot or a drawn weapon: the half second in which they have witnessed it

crowd-startle-fearful-ticks.src: brief 011 fight AI §4; GDD §04 Fearful; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4 (Motive owns the number)
crowd-startle-fearful-ticks.reason: a Fearful person bolts first: two ticks. Readable, from a field the player can learn (temperament)

crowd-run-cm-s.src: brief 011 fight AI §4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4 (Motive owns the number)
crowd-run-cm-s.reason: a civilian runs a little slower than an operative (280): a fleeing person is never faster than the cell

crowd-flee-max-cm.src: brief 011 fight AI §4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4 (Motive owns the number)
crowd-flee-max-cm.reason: the refuge a person runs to is within 40 m

crowd-quiet-s.src: brief 011 fight AI §4; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4 (Motive owns the number)
crowd-quiet-s.reason: people come back 30 s after the last shot

crowd-occlude-cm.src: GDD §05 crowds block guard and camera sightlines; Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4 (Motive owns the number)
crowd-occlude-cm.reason: a person on the street blocks a watcher's sightline that passes within 30 cm of them (a body 60 cm across, head height above the eye); hostiles' own sight ignores people, and a shot never hits one

drive-slack-cm.src: brief 025 playground (Sky 2026-10-19, take control); Keel, briefs/024/keel-wasd.md §2
drive-slack-cm.reason: EXPERIMENTAL. A driven sample may lie this much beyond the distance its budget allows: rounding between the host's floats and the engine's centimetres

drive-burst-ticks.reason: EXPERIMENTAL. A driven agent's distance budget refills one tick of its pace each tick and holds at most this many ticks of it: a host whose frames straddle ticks may hand two ticks' walk in one sample, never more

drive-busy-push-cm.src: brief 025 playground (moving a busy agent cancels the action at its cancel cost); Keel, briefs/024/keel-wasd.md §1
drive-busy-push-cm.reason: EXPERIMENTAL. Pushing a busy agent this far in all (summed over the ticks it pushes) cancels the action in progress, as the cancel order does; less is pinned

drive-gap-cm.src: brief 025 playground (people keep a 40 cm gap from the driven agent)
drive-gap-cm.reason: EXPERIMENTAL. A driven step that would end nearer a person on the street than this, and nearer than they were, is not taken (sliding along an axis where that clears it); stepping away is always allowed. 0 turns it off

lab-health-scale.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-health-scale.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. every weapons.health is multiplied by this at the start, so damage can differ by weapon (a sidearm takes 10 of a rival's 30); integers throughout

lab-sidearm-damage.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-sidearm-damage.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the sidearm's damage a hit (health ×10)

lab-sidearm-every-ticks.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-sidearm-every-ticks.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the sidearm fires every 1.0 s (medium); was 0.6 s: two trained officers dropped an op in 1.1 s, under the 2.5 s floor (Motive tuning, briefs/027/motive/tuning.md)

lab-sidearm-eff-m.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-sidearm-eff-m.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the sidearm's effective ring, today's 15 m; hostiles engage only inside it, and at 12 m police never fired back while the cell hit them from 20 m (Motive tuning, briefs/027/motive/tuning.md)

lab-sidearm-max-m.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-sidearm-max-m.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the sidearm's max ring: 1 m past the effective ring, so the cell's free long band (shooting what can't shoot back) is short; was 18, Motive's §6.6 fallback taken after Suture's second retest (retest2.md N1: at 18 a band runner downed the final fight's police without being fired on) (Motive tuning, briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §6.6)

lab-sidearm-arms.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-sidearm-arms.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. a sidearm takes 1 Arms in the loadout

lab-carbine-damage.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-carbine-damage.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the carbine's damage a hit

lab-carbine-every-ticks.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-carbine-every-ticks.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the carbine fires every 0.8 s

lab-carbine-eff-m.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the carbine's effective ring, as today

lab-carbine-max-m.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-carbine-max-m.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the carbine's max ring, as today

lab-carbine-arms.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-carbine-arms.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the carbine is the cell's: it takes no Arms

lab-carbine-charge.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-carbine-charge.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the carbine pays 20 charge a shot: 5 shots from a full cell, then it waits on regen (Keel 027 proposal 4: make the charge bite); no matrix run binds it, judged in play (Motive tuning, briefs/027/motive/tuning.md)

lab-machine-damage.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-machine-damage.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the machine pistol's damage a hit

lab-machine-every-ticks.src: brief 027 playground (Sky 2026-10-20: try three fight modes in the playground); Motive, briefs/027/playground.md §2
lab-machine-every-ticks.reason: EXPERIMENTAL: brief 027 playground. the machine pistol fires every 0.3 s (very fast; Motive's 0.25 s rounded to whole ticks)

standing.rule: One integer per district, starting at `start` (one step short of the Hero band: Sky 2026-10-16, 'Hero is kinda the default'). At or above `hero` the district is in the Hero band, at or below `menace` in the Menace band, otherwise neutral. In a mission only acts seen or found move it: each witnessed incident of a Hero act adds one `step`, of a Menace act takes one (traceable[].standing, witness.sees), a public fight moves it once when it ends, by whom the cell fought (fight.public, Sky 2026-10-16: 'it should be per fight, and depends who you're fighting'; not capped, and a move for the drift), and a found killing moves it takedown.foundKillStanding; a missing person moves nothing. Facts along ties never move it (Sky Q6). Between missions the word does (standing.word): each person the cell helped, pressured or knocked out this mission, alive, not missing and with a tie of a kind in `word.ties`, tells those ties how a stranger treated them, once per person, not per tie: helped +`word.step`, pressured or knocked out −`word.step`; a person both helped and harmed counts as harmed (a threat outweighs a kindness). The word's net move in a district is clamped to ±`word.cap` a mission; seen and found acts are never capped. The word is a feeling, not a fact: no face, place or time and nothing about the cell goes with it, so it is no fact for word.passes, the Talker test or the investigators, and word-quiet-loyalty does not stop it. Then (standing.drift) a district where nothing moved Standing this mission (no act seen or found, in the mission or after it, and no word) moves `drift` back toward `start`, from either side, never past it. The debrief carries one Standing line per district (debrief.lines.standing) with its cause, one of `causes`: the cause that moved it most toward the net change (the earliest on a tie), `balanced` when the moves cancel, a drift, or `steady`. Heat (§06) = campaign Trail + max(0, −standing), unchanged: from the start it takes 3 net Menace steps before Standing adds Heat, and Hero never cancels Trail; its threshold is Motive's.

Violence seen by a civilian sets violenceSeen at once. Alert never falls within a mission.

memory.rule: A memory entry is {act, by, place, time, witnessed} (Motive K1). `by` is the face of the operative who did the act: a face is only an id (Adams 2017), and only the Fixer's face is a fact (people.rules talker.facts; §03 the face witnesses remember), so an entry whose `by` is a key of faceFacts also yields that fact. `witnessed` = a third person saw the act. Only a `remember` change writes memory, only acts listed here, only on simulated people (people.rules tiers; Sky Q5). A told entry carries the fact it was told and is never retold (one hop). The facts a person holds are the union over their entries; people.rules talker.lie's `helped` is an entry of act `help`; a remembered refusal is an entry of act `refusal`. An entry yields its act's facts as listed here, plus the face fact of `by` (faceFacts). Brief 013 (Sky D3): the Enforcer's face is a fact, scoped to the new acts: a witness of a takedown (saw-takedown) and a victim who saw him coming (attacked-aware) hold enforcer-face; older entries by the Enforcer (a run, a shot, a drawn weapon) keep yielding place and time only, so every recorded run's debrief stands.

privacy.rule: A turning conversation is private (Sky 2026-10-16). An event marked private (Listen, Ask, Pay, Help) has no witnesses: onlookers within witness range learn nothing from it, so it makes no witness fact or memory, no witness Trail, no Standing move, no incident for the investigators, nothing told along ties and no word between missions, and its card counts nobody who would see it. The event's own price stands: its base Trail (Pay is still traceable money), its time and cash, and the subject's own memory and report (a Loyal person still reports an approach). Pressure is not private: a threat is visible, and onlookers see it, remember it and pass it on (witness.sees). Every event by the Fixer or the Scout says whether it is private; a private event may carry no witnesses. Watch is no conversation (not private) and no traceable act (no witnesses): watching someone shows nothing. The traceable acts payment and debt-cleared stay in `traceable` for a visible act that is not a conversation; no turning verb makes them now.

drive.experimental: brief 025 playground (Sky 2026-10-19): take control of an agent and move them freely. Not a design decision: the GDD (v0.24) is unchanged until Sky has played it; every switch below may change or the section go.
drive.rule: EXPERIMENTAL (brief 025). A driven agent is moved by the host (a character controller) and handed to the engine as drive samples, one an operative a tick at most, each an order in the log: {do: drive, to: [x, y] cm, run: true for Shift, face: degrees} and {do: drive, release: true}. The first sample takes control: a walk in progress ends (kept for a resume on release). Each tick the engine moves the agent toward its sample: at most its distance budget (refilled each tick by the pace it may move at: cell.speed, or cell.runSpeed for a run, a carrier's walk while carrying, cell.speed while a run is refused as a move's run is; held at `burst` ticks of it) plus `slack`; then over the walk grid one axis at a time (x, then y), each stopped at the first blocked cell, so it slides along walls and never crosses one; then a step that would end within `gap` of a person on the street and nearer than they were is not taken (an axis alone is tried). The engine's position is the agent's: the host reads it back. Everything else reads the agent where it stands (sight, witnesses, reach, the tether, the loop, Vale beside the Enforcer). A run is one span, from the first run sample to a walk sample or release, however its heading turns: running is noticed as a move's run is (cell.runAlert once a span), and a run ends a fire order. A busy agent (an act in progress): onBusy `cancel`: pushing it `busyPush` in all cancels the act at the cancel line's cost (rulebook cancel); `hold`: it stands until the act lands. Down, inside, in the car or carried, control ends. A click move ends control; acts given while driven are taken where the agent stands (no walk to reach). Release: onRelease `stand`: the agent stands where left; `resume`: the walk control took over goes on from here. A playground start may set pace (per mille of every pace), onBusy, onRelease and gap (Start.drive), hashed with the start state.

cell.rule: The cell's verbs other than Turn, Watch and Listen (§03): how long each takes, how near the operative must stand, the Trail it leaves. An act on a device or a door (Loop and Reroute at the cabinet, Enter at the public door, Board at the getaway car) is done at it, within `atReach`; acts on people keep `reach` (Sky 2026-10-15 playtest). Carry: an operative lifts a downed one in `carry`, then walks only and doesn't fire. Board and Go (brief 018, Sky 2026-10-18): Board is an order on the getaway car, given within `atReach` of it, not running, not tethered, not mid-action, not carrying a body; it takes `board.s`, and `carry.s` more when carrying (the carried go in first: Vale, only the Enforcer carries him, or a downed operative). An operative in the car is off the street and doesn't fire, and is a target as one still beside cover (weapons.mod.cover); a move on a boarded operative steps out at the car's side in `board.s`, then walks; Vale stays in. Go, given by anyone once someone is in the car, is refused while the car is held (fight.hold) and names the holders; the car leaves at once with whoever is inside and the mission ends. The win is Vale in the car when it leaves; Go without him is the cell withdrawing by car. Left behind at Go: a downed operative not in the car is captured (why downed); a standing one is captured if a combatant is still up and not broken (fighting) or the seal clock runs (sealed), else walks out and is back next mission (walked). Captures happen only at Go; a failed mission and the menu's Withdraw capture nobody. Seen leaving: a police officer, a robot or an engaged patrol up and with the car in its cone or within witness range on a clear line (a final-fight officer: a clear line within weapons.pistol.max, brief 018 §10) makes the departure one witnessed incident (witness-trail) and gives the investigation the car (cell-car, a hunted car next mission); rivals don't report. No auto-board: standing at the car is not boarding. An order takes its time and lands at its end; a Call lands at once (the top-down test's spill: the guard walks from the call). Running (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md): a move with run at runSpeed; refused while carrying Vale or a downed operative, while the Tech holds a loop, or while doing an action; a runner is noticed where an act would be: people remember where and when (and the Fixer's face), security that sees it counts a found fault (runAlert, once per run). Running is free while a fight is on. Enter takes enter.alarm longer once Alert ≥ 2 (the staff hide Vale). Loop: the cabinet loops one camera at a time, one of `loop.targets` (a camera of the site by id, or `world`: the city's own cameras, the Records Square mast); the pickup camera joined the list on Sky's answer 6 (2026-10-16: "if the tech takes out the camera, then taking out the guard and driver is possible"; Waymark, briefs/013/waymark-handover.md §5.1).
cell.src: §03 cell; §07 route timings; the top-down test; Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md

security.rule: Who answers gunfire and how fast. A report calls the response unit (`weapons.health.responseOfficers` officers); the earliest arrival wins and the district seals after it arrives (the seal is the security level's, `response.levels`). The delay is by who reported: a civilian witness, a guard, camera or patrol that saw it, nobody (unseen), a civilian shot. These delays are the arrivals at security level 1 (routine, today's 12 s dispatch): at another level a report lands the same seconds after the shot and the unit rolls that level's dispatch later, so the arrival moves by the dispatch's difference. A downed guard is missed at his next check-in mark (`response.checkIn`; brief 013 retires the 18 s check-in). Gunfire draws the rivals within `rivals.drawn` and the patrol within `patrol.breakTo`. A hostile who first sees the cell outside a fight reacts in `weapons.react`, then fires at its weapon's cadence (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: replaces aim 3 s and the per-unit fire rates).
security.src: §05 security [B], rivals [B]; §06 prototype [B]; the top-down test (Suture M-3: the rulebook carries them, src the prototype)

weapons.settle: A shooter whose run ends (it stands or walks again, after a click run or a driven run that moved) waits `aimNew` before its next shot: its next shot is no sooner than aimNew after the tick the run ends. It keeps its target, its fire order and the pair's accumulator (a reset would hand back the reset-kite exploit). The same for every shooter that runs (today only the cell runs). No new value: today's aimNew, the lab's fight.lab.aimNew. Sky 2026-10-21 (the settle, a direction Sky approved; Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §10.2), engine 0.16.0, both presets.
weapons.trigger: The driven agent fires with its trigger (tuning.md §11, Sky on firing 2026-10-21, brief 024): a logged input (op, on or off, target, tick). Pressed, it fires at its target on the weapon's cadence while it has reach and a line; a press fires exactly one shot at the first ready tick, a press in the cooldown is never dropped and buys that one shot only (a buffer of one, not a queue), lost if the agent aims at something else, the target goes, or it has no reach or line when the gun is ready. Released, it keeps its target and its count: a press on the same target fires on cadence with no aimNew and no reset (no tap reset). A press ends the agent's own fire order (the trigger takes over); a fire order given to it ends the trigger; control ending clears it. A lock is a lasting fire order; a locked agent is engaged, and so is an agent returning fire on its own shooter (a draw sets stance return, never at will; in the lab too since tuning.md §13.4). Follow: a cell agent that is drawn, not locked, not holding (hold fires only when ordered: a holding agent never follows and is never locked by a press, tuning.md §13.2), not returning fire, not busy, not carrying, not inside or in the car, standing within `follow` of the driven agent, with its own reach and line to the target, follows: it never walks and never draws to follow, and joins as any new target is taken (aimNew, the settle). With the follow setting off, followers fire at the target only while the trigger is held and keep their aim on release; on, a press or a change of target while pressed locks each follower at that tick (a fire order with its walk-in spent: it lapses `lineLapse` out of line and never walks). The engine derives the followers in operative id order with integer distances and logs them (fire.follow, fire.lock); the setting is the start's followLock or a logged follow order.
weapons.rule: Who carries what and how a shot lands (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md). The Enforcer carries the carbine (the cell's); every other operative may carry a pistol, one per `sidearmArms` of Arms (the Handover issues all three); the guard, the patrol, officers and rivals carry pistols; the Enforcer, officers, the guard and the patrol are trained. A shot's accuracy is its band's (inside `pointBlank`, inside the weapon's eff, inside its max) times each modifier that applies, in per mille: the shooter's gait this tick (tuning.md §8.3, Sky 2026-10-21: a walk `mod.moving`, a run toward or across `mod.running`, a run away, its step within `runAwayCone` degrees of straight away from the target, `mod.runningAway`), the target still beside cover (`mod.cover`; with `pointBlankCover` false, never inside `pointBlank`: Sky 2026-10-21, tuning.md §8.4, as the lab) or, for a target running this tick past point blank, `mod.targetRunning` in its place (one step, never with cover), the Enforcer holding Vale (`mod.vale`), an untrained shooter (`mod.untrained`). Hits are deterministic: each shooter keeps an integer accumulator on each target, the pair's for the mission (tuning.md §13.1, engine 0.18.0, as the lab's aim memory): taking a target resumes the count the shooter left on it and nothing resets it (a switch, cease, hold, holster, a release); a target it has not fired at starts at `acc.start`; each shot adds the accuracy, and at 1000 or more the shot hits and 1000 comes off (750: exactly three in four). A shot does the weapon's damage; health per kind is `health`, at 0 down. The cost moves from the shot to the victim: +`costs.gunfire` T once per shooting (the first shot at each target, hit or miss), +`costs.hit` T per person hit, once, and +`costs.down` more when they go down; the final fight stays untraced (fight.traced). A drawn weapon seen by security raises Alert to `costs.drawSeenSecurity` and that watcher engages; seen by people, it is one witnessed incident (Alert at least `costs.drawSeenPeople`, standing per traceable weapon-drawn), and drawings within `costs.drawWindow` and witness range of it are the same incident (Motive addendum 2026-10-15). Fire on the move (tuning.md §8.2): a fire order stops a walker (it stands and fires, or walks in when out of reach or line) and never stops a runner (the run goes on, firing at its gait; out of reach it walks in once the run ends); a driven agent keeps its drive and fires at each tick's gait; a move given while a fire order stands keeps the order and fires on the move, and spends its walk-in (out of reach when the move ends, it holds its aim `lineLapse` and lapses; a new fire order walks in again); stances fire at the gait's chance. Anyone can be shot (tuning.md §9, Sky 2026-10-21) but the cell's own agents. Orders: draw (`draw` ticks), holster (`holster`), stance (hold, return, free), fire until down (first shot `aimNew` after taking the target; holds aim `lineLapse` when the line breaks), cease, panic (once a fight is on). A civilian or a contact is a target only when the order says so (the Ctrl case: the ring's Fire always says so). Tuning.md §9 (engine 0.15.0): Vale, a final-fight hostile after fight.over, a knocked-out or restrained person where they lie (a hit kills them: a takedown kill's consequences plus the gunfire's), a response unit or robot by its own id and a camera ("camera:<id>", `health.camera`; shot out it is dark for the mission; gunfire only: no hit or down Trail, no Standing) are all targets; a person shot down outside the final fight lies dead where they fell (a brief-013 body); the cell's own agents are the one target refusal (fire-on-cell). An order whose shot would fail the mission (Vale; the driver while Vale is out) always takes the `costs.loudHold` hold. Brief 030 (Sky 2026-10-20): `close`: a fire order on a target out of the weapon's reach, or with no clear line, walks the grid (at a walk) to the nearest free point inside its effective reach with a clear line (within 60 m of walk; none: refused out-of-range or no-clear-line), stands there and fires; it holds while it walks (no lapse), and a driven agent is not walked (the host drives; the order holds). `autoHolster`: a weapon drawn by a fire order or by panic (not by a draw order) is holstered by the engine `autoHolster` seconds after the fight it was drawn for ends (fight.public: quiet after its last shot, the final fight at fight.over), unless the agent still has a fire order, a stance order was given since the draw, or a hostile combatant up within its weapon's max reach has a clear line to the agent (then at the first tick none has); a weapon drawn with a draw order stays drawn until holstered.
weapons.reason: Sky approved Motive's five answers on 2026-10-15; the numbers are Motive's calculator's (briefs/011/motive-fights/fights.py), [S] until Suture's frontier runs on the engine.

ai.rule: What a hostile does in a fight (Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §2–3; Sky approved real-time shoot-outs, briefs/011/motive-fights.md). One machine: routine, alerted (react; summoned bodies skip it; an ambush waits weapons.aimNew, plus fight.safe.warn if Inez warned), advance (to the cover point the site's cover data gives, else to stopReach of its weapon's effective reach short of its foe or objective; fires as it moves, at weapons.mod for its gait: tuning.md §8.3, Sky 2026-10-21, both presets), engage (a foe inside its effective reach on a clear line: stops, takes its target by class: 1 whoever fired at it within weapons.lineLapse (for a police body, any operative who did, not only the last: tuning.md §12.2; the target it aims at stays while its shooter keeps firing), 2 the operative holding Vale, 3 the nearest with a weapon drawn, 4 the nearest; keeps it until down, out of reach or sight for lineLapse, or a better class appears; a new target costs aimNew; steps to cover when unprotected, once each cover.stepGap, and leaves a point unprotected for cover.leave; cover.stepFires (true): that step fires at the walk's chance; false is tuning.md §8.3's fallback, measured and not adopted: a rival walking to the cover it stepped to, and an operative on a cover-snap walk, fire nothing; advances, closes and lanes still fire), hold (holders: police, the patrol, a guard; a target reacquired within reacquire is shot at once), break (rivals: more than half the crew down; they run for their car and are gone within rivalGone; no longer combatants, no longer hold the car, no Trail), down. Lapse to hold or advance after engageLapse with no foe in reach. A body beside a cover point (cover.snap) that shields it, standing still, past point blank, is hit at weapons.mod.cover (quality ≥ qFull) or modPartial (≥ qPartial). One body to a cover point. Seek: how far each looks for cover. Police (officers) hold their stand and never break; the response unit joins the loud fight at the nearest police stand (overflow beside a taken one, else the nearest free cover within seek.police); the guard ally runs to his post, taking cover within seek.ally; an engaging guard fights from where he stands and stands down guardReturn after his last foe; the patrol chases to the shot's origin and resumes its sweep patrolResume after its last foe. Shots resolve together at the end of a tick. The crowd's scatter (Pulse §4) is not in yet.
ai.src: Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (brief 011); Sky 2026-10-15 approved Motive's briefs/011/motive-fights.md
ai.reason: Pulse's spec, every number his proposal and Motive's to tune; the crowd's values wait for the crowd's states.

crowd.rule: The crowd in a fight (Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4). A person of the city's people on the street is startled by a shot whose shooter stands within `scatter`, seen or not, or by an operative's drawn weapon within witness range on a clear line: they stand `startle` ticks (a Fearful person `startleFearful`), then flee at `run` by the grid to a refuge of the site's cover data (a door or a street mouth) within `fleeMax` that ends farther from the shooter than they stand, the nearest (ties on id), or if none the refuge farthest from the shooter; there they are sheltered, off the street. `quiet` after the last shot they walk back to the stop their routine has for the clock. Witnesses are taken at the shot, before any startle: a person within witness range with a clear line to the shooter or the target remembers saw-gunfire (place, time, the face). Nobody is hit by a stray shot. A person on the street who is not sheltered blocks a watcher's sightline (the guard, the patrol, a camera, the response unit) that passes within `occlude` of them, between two bodies' width of either end; a hostile's own aim ignores people. The four people the Handover casts by role keep their roles: they do not scatter.
crowd.src: Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4; §06 citizen actions; §05 crowds block guard and camera sightlines
crowd.reason: Pulse's spec; the cast by role keep their places so the mission's contacts stay where its rules need them (Keel).

summon.rule: The summons (Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md §1.3): a turned contact who is called sends for their lover (people.rules ties.kinds.lover), read from the city's ties, never from the mission. The lover leaves where he is, walks the grid to the caller at walking pace (cell.speed), stays `stay` and walks back. Refused, at no cost and with its code, when he is off the street, busy (down, held, engaged in a fight, or already away), more than `walkMax` away, Alert is above `alertMax`, he holds a memory of the cell's gunfire, violence or drawn weapon, or he has come `perShift` times this shift. Alert reaching above `alertMax` ends the visit: he runs back at security's pace. The visit is no act of the cell: the call keeps cell.call.trail. A contact's role job (the driver's camera block) is the call's other use. `together`: a Watch that ends with two lovers within it teaches the cell their affair (people.rules secrets).
summon.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door
summon.reason: systems over scripts: any turned contact with an eligible lover is a lure, in every generated mission (Motive §1.3). Keel models the visit for a lover with a post (the guard), as the Handover needs; another lover is refused until a routine can be left.

cancel.rule: A cancel order stops what one operative is doing now, the activity the HUD shows: an act in progress first, then a walk or run, then a fire order, then a draw, then a loop held, then a downed operative carried. Each verb's line says what cancelling it costs or keeps. stop: the operative stands where they are. holster: a draw not yet done goes back. cease: the fire order ends, the weapon stays drawn. lost: the act's time is spent and nothing lands (Watch and Listen learn nothing; a Loop, Reroute, Mislead or lift not finished does nothing; their Trail is charged only when they land). aborted: the approach stops mid-conversation; the money held for it comes back (the engine holds the price at the order and pays it only in the outcome's charge, Redline E2), no Trail, and the person remembers an aborted approach (memory act `aborted`, with the Fixer's face): it is no refusal, so the approach may be tried again, but it is a fact an investigator can get. ends: the loop stops and the camera comes back. staff-report: the Enforcer comes back out without Vale by the public door, or by the service door if a unit holds the public door, or waits inside while both are held (response; brief 013 E3); the Office staff report the intruder, one reported incident (alert.byIncident). vale-reports: Vale is let go at his car and reports the attempt, one reported incident, and he remembers the aborted take (memory act `aborted`, the Enforcer's face), so an investigator who questions him finds a lead (Motive addendum Q4). put-down: the carried operative is laid down where the carrier stands. Go is instant and has nothing to cancel; a Board or a step-out cancelled spends the time and lands nothing (lost). Putting Vale down is no cancel: the Enforcer keeps him (a rule of its own if Sky wants one). The verbs whose line may change take one of: turn aborted or lost; enter staff-report or quiet; take vale-reports or quiet. Brief 013: a takedown cancelled before it lands lets the victim go (`takedown` released): he saw the Enforcer and reports it as a woken victim would; lifting, dropping, stashing or tying a body cancelled spends the time and lands nothing (`body` lost); a body carried is laid down where the carrier stands (`carrying` put-down).
cancel.src: Sky 2026-10-15 playtest: "there's nothing showing me what the cell player is doing when they're busy, nor is there a way to cancel their action" (Aster)
cancel.reason: Accepted by Motive (addendum 2026-10-15 Q4; no put-Vale-down rule in the Handover). Keel's proposal: cancelling an act already under way spends its time and lands nothing, as a refusal does; the money held comes back because it was never handed over; the two acts that put a stranger in front of someone (Enter, Take) leave a report, as an interrupted intrusion would; a broken-off approach leaves the person the Fixer's face but no refusal, so cancel is no free retry of a bad card but no punishment like a refusal either.

perception.rule: A watcher sees a point inside its cone (ahead within reach, and to the side within half × ahead ÷ reach), along a sightline no occluder crosses at eye height (§05 levels: 3D). A person (a walking guard, the response's officers, the rivals) also sees anyone within `near` whatever their facing; a machine (a camera, the patrol, sweeping or chasing, the response's robots) sees by its cone only (brief 031 L2, Sky 2026-10-20: "robots look futuristic, mindset is still quite old school, forward facing cameras not 360"). The guard posted at his door has no near sense for detection (his door cone only); the attention clock gives him one (attention.near). A camera's cone is its site's; a guard at his door, a walking guard, a chasing patrol, the response unit and the rivals use these. The sweeping patrol's cone widens with depth.
perception.src: §05 cameras, watchers, levels; the top-down test's cones

sight.rule: What the cell knows of each watcher's sight (Sky 2026-10-16: cones are the Scout's skill; brief 031, Sky 2026-10-20: every agent watches). A watcher's sight is its perception cone clipped by what blocks sight; the cell knows it only once learned, and learned knowledge stays with the cell (a downed Scout keeps it). learn watch: a completed Watch (cell.watch, watch.s, $0, 0 T, no Alert of its own) of the watcher by any operative in its kind's `by` (all four) teaches its sight. The reach is the agent's, watch.reach by operative, one ring for people and machines alike, on a clear line at eye height (walls, solids and people on the street block it); every watcher teaches the same facts. The Tech does not Watch while his loop holds (he is tethered to the cabinet). The guard is watched as the person he is (cell.watch: routine), and that Watch teaches his sight too. Listen and Mislead stay the Scout's. What anyone learns is the cell's. learn arrival: the response unit and drawn rivals come for the cell, and their sight is known from the moment they are on the street. Knowledge is witnessed (watched) or told (the start state: the briefing, a previous mission). routine fixed: a camera does not move, so its routine is known with its sight; person: the guard's routine is his person routine (cell.watch); watched: the patrol's routine (when its sweep turns and when it sees the door) is known once the union of the cell's completed Watches of it, in mission time, reaches watch.routine seconds (two agents watching at once count once); none: no routine. Knowledge changes only what the cards show, never an outcome: a quote's 'seen by' shows each known watcher's true answer, and `unknown` for a watcher the cell doesn't know that stands within its kind's farthest sight of the act or route on a clear line (its facing is what the cell doesn't know), as the action card shows '?' until the temperament is known (§04, Sky Q3). Detection needs no knowledge: a watcher that sees an operative now has noticed them, known or not.
sight.src: Sky 2026-10-16 (Aster): view cones are the Scout's skill; Sky 2026-10-18 (Aster): "tech should be able to watch camera / robots like scout can"; brief 031 (Sky 2026-10-20): "all characters should be able to watch", reach per agent (Motive, briefs/031-everyone-watches.md §1) (the machines' `by`; people stay the Scout's); Glyph, briefs/011/ui/review-2026-10-16 §3.4; §03 Scout: Watch; §04 preview '?' (Sky Q3); §05 cameras, watchers
sight.reason: the GDD has every cone always on (§05 cameras: fixed visible cones). Sky approved the Scout's skill on 2026-10-16; the reach, the routine's time and the known-on-arrival rule are Keel's starting values, for Motive to price and Sky's GDD edit.

attention.rule: Watchers notice loiterers (brief 031 §2; Sky 2026-10-20: "standing in an observed area for a while without moving causes alert. So standing behind a camera's LoS is fine"). Every security watcher on the street keeps one clock per operative: each live camera (not looped, not blocked), the door guard (not the cell's ally), the patrol robot and the response's officers and robots; civilians and rivals keep none. Each tick, for each operative on the street (not inside, not in the car, not down or carried): in the watcher's sight and standing still, idle or Watching, the clock runs +1 s a second; in sight in any other act (Listen, a turn, Call, Loop, Reroute, Mislead, Enter, Take, a takedown, carrying a body or Vale, restraining, stashing: Sky L1) it holds; moving, or out of its sight, it drains 1 s a second, to 0, or to the wary mark once wary. In sight (`sense`): a machine (cone) by its perception cone only; a person (near) by his cone and anyone within `near` on a clear line whatever his facing, the guard posted at his door included (for the clock only: a takedown's awareness at the order keeps his cone). People on the street block sight. The marks are the band's (by the cell's Heat, read once at the mission's start from the start state's `heat`, else the mission's start.heat, else 0; the band is the last whose heatFrom the Heat reaches): at `notice` the watcher has noticed the operative (a warning only); at `wary` it is wary of him for the rest of the mission (its clock never drains below the wary mark again; a wary person is aware of him at a takedown: unarmed he struggles, the armed guard draws); at `report` it reports a loiterer, once per operative per watcher per mission: a camera's report lands at its watcher's next scan (`report.scan`, phase from the camera's id, as witness.cameraScan) plus `report.call`; a person's or a robot's by radio after `report.call`; a person or robot downed before it lands drops it. A loiterer reported is a found fault: Alert to at least `alert`, no Trail, logged as a sighting (watcher, operative, place, time), and the dial dispatches its response for the Alert reached (an alarm with no body: counts topped up, never repeated). Heat = campaign Trail + Menace (max(0, −Standing)), fixed for the mission (§05).
attention.src: brief 031 §2 (approved by Sky 2026-10-20: D1, D3, L1, L2, L3); Motive, briefs/031-everyone-watches.md; probe briefs/031/loiter-probe-heat0.txt
attention.reason: generous at the start (the Handover is Heat 0: a 20 s Watch from inside a sight line just reaches wary, only a 45 s stand reports); wary within a Watch's 20 s in every band, so a whole Watch in sight always makes the watcher wary (D1); only when infamous is the report (18 s) shorter than a Watch. Tuned by play.

takedown.rule: The Enforcer's takedown (brief 013, Sky 2026-10-16: anyone can be targeted; one rule set for every simulated person, no named target list). The Enforcer alone, standing within `reach` of a person on the street, knocks them out (`ko`) or kills them (`kill`); silent: none of the gunfire rules apply, no money. Vale may be killed (the mission fails, §07) but not knocked out (use Take); the patrol and cameras are no targets (Reroute and Loop are their verbs). A target who had the Enforcer in his cone when the order was given, heard him running within witness range, or witnessed one of the cell's acts this mission (a takedown, a carry, a drawn weapon: Motive rev 3, until a stop has a facing) is aware: unarmed, he struggles (`struggle` more), screams (heard within witness.scream) and holds the Enforcer's face; armed (a person with a weapon: the door guard), the takedown fails, he draws and engages (Alert at least weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity at sight). The victim lies where he fell until moved: a body. A knocked-out victim wakes after `wake`, staggers `stagger`, then reports the assault whatever his temperament (a cell contact says nothing); a dead one never wakes or talks. Any operative carries a body (cell.carry lift, then walk only: the Enforcer at cell.speed, the others at carry.untrained; no run, no fire) and puts it down in carry.drop; restrains a living one in `restrain` (no move, no call-out, still seen on open ground; a finder frees him in `free`, then he reports); stashes it, standing at the stash, into a container (`stash.container`, on the street, seen as a carry) or through a service door (`stash.door`, off-screen; a door holds `stash.doorHolds` bodies, a storeroom: rev 4 R4.3; a container what its site entry says). Only a stash hides a body (two hide levels, open and shut; Sky merged call 6). A woken, unrestrained victim in a stash calls out every `callOut`, heard within witness.scream. A container is emptied by a round every `service.period`, its phase from its id, standing `service.dwell`: a body inside is found then (in the mission only; Sky merged call 9). Every number of the takedown, the price and its forecast are on the order's card before it is given.

witness.rule: What a person does when the city's silent violence reaches them (Pulse's decision list; Motive's numbers). Who notices: a takedown or a carry, everyone on the street within witness range on a clear line at any tick of it; an open body, the same, checked every `check.ticks` (phase from the body's id); a live camera, the guard, the patrol and the response's units in their cones; a shut body nobody. The rows, first that holds, evaluated when the person notices: staff (a job in `staff`, or the door guard): radio from where he stands, landing react + postCall (the armed guard, the patrol and the response's units seeing an act or a carry engage instead: Alert at least weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity at sight); kin of the victim (a tie in `kin`): report at once, whatever the temperament (fear `terrifiedFear`: flee); cell (turned, or loyalty at least values.word-quiet-loyalty): quiet; an Informer (resentment at its max): report; terrified (fear at least `terrifiedFear`): flee, never report; then by temperament: Loyal reports; Idealist reports, after walking to a body to learn its state (`check`); Mercenary reports only once Alert is at least `mercenaryAlert`; Fearful flees an act or carry and avoids a body. A reporter walks the grid to the nearest report point (a staffed door: the site's door refuges; a call box), at walking pace for a body and running pace (crowd.run) for an act or a carry, and calls (`call`): the report lands at the desk; a live camera's lands at its next scan (`cameraScan`, phase from its id) + postCall; a robot's after `robot`. At most `cap` reporters of one incident are in transit; one taken down, killed or carried before his report lands drops it. Whoever quiets, avoids or flees, and every reporter, tells one tie (first kind in `tells`): a tie on the street within `tell` face to face at once; a tie indoors at a unit only from a phone (calls are voice, no networks: GDD §01; Aster 2026-10-16, brief 013 E1). A reporter who walked to a report point tells from its phone when the report lands; one who radios tells face to face only, unless he stands at a report point. A quiet or avoiding person with no tie in speaking range and a tie indoors walks to the nearest report point and calls (`call`), the same walk as a report and stopped the same way (taken down, or Vale taken, before the call: nobody is told); a fleeing one calls only if the refuge her flight ends at is a staffed door. A tell is no report: it is outside `cap` and raises no Alert. A told entry, facts only, one hop (a told person never tells it on); a told Loyal person reports it from where they are. Alert rises when a report lands, never at sight (Sky merged call 1), to `alert` by what it says: a takedown seen `seen`, a carry seen `carry`, a person lying (or a noise from a stash) `down`, a dead body (staff know, an Idealist checks) `dead`, a woken victim `woken`, a missed check-in `mark`, a missing expected person `missing`; a knockout never above takedown.koAlertMax by itself; one takedown is one incident (Alert to the highest of its landed and confirmed reports; the nth reported incident at least alert.byIncident[n-1]). Witness Trail (+values.witness-trail) and Standing (traceable takedown) move once per incident at sight; a turned witness (loyalty at least values.word-quiet-loyalty) adds no Trail, and Standing still moves (Sky merged call 5). A screaming witness (fear at least `screamFear`), kin and an aware victim are heard within `scream` with no line: hearers with a line within witness range become witnesses; the rest hold heard-alarm. A reporter volunteers place and time when questioned (investigator.question, outcome volunteers). Rev 4 (Motive R4.2; Sky 2026-10-16): before every row, an accomplice of the act (a person turned to enable this very act: for the Take and its escort, the turned driver) is never its witness, whatever the tie; `kin` is lover or family only (workmate is not kin; `close`, lover, family and workmate, is whose absence or loss a person feels: expectations, the alarm's places, grief and worry). The Take: at Vale's own car with its driver turned it happens inside the car, off-screen, with no witness window (and nothing for the pickup camera to see); any other Take reads as an act for its first cell.take.struggle s, seen as a takedown by everyone within witness range on a clear line and every watcher that sees him (a live pickup camera still fails it at the order, §07). Escorted on foot, Vale looks wrong only to his kin within witness range on a clear line, or to anyone within values.near-m on a clear line who sees the grip: a carry seen. The Take and its escort are one incident, opened at the first sighting (an unseen Take opens none); witness Trail and Standing move at sight; no assault Trail is charged (the Take keeps cell.take.trailUnturned); Vale let go by a cancel reports on the same incident if it was seen.

response.rule: The response is a dial (Sky 2026-10-16: 'it's easy to swarm the play area with robots'; merged call 3): `levels` indexed by the security level S = the district's base + its open cases (campaign) + the mission's bonus, from the mission's data; the Handover's is 2. A landed alarm (a report of a silent act, a missed check-in, a missing person; gunfire, whose report lands its security.response delay less level 1's dispatch after the shot) puts the response on the street the level's `dispatch` later: at Alert 1 `a1Robots` robots; at Alert 2 or more `a2Units` units of weapons.health.responseOfficers officers (the response unit first) and `a2Robots` robots, then one more unit every `reinforce` up to `unitCap`; Alert 3 adds `a3Units` units to the district mouths (the cordon) and, where `doorsLock`, the doors lock (no Enter). A found body holds the scene (rev 4, Motive R4.1; Sky 2026-10-16): a landed report that a person lies there (down, dead, a takedown seen), the body still there and open, or a woken victim's own report where he woke, brings a unit of officers at any Alert (not bound by robot reach; not one of the dial's counted units; at Alert 2 the response unit is it), the level's dispatch after the landing. The scene holds the entrance the body lies at (within values.near-m) and every entrance within witness range of it on a clear line: from an officer's arrival (its check and its `search.s` sweep, opening stashes only at Alert 2 or more) until the unit stands down (the timers below), a held entrance refuses Enter (`door-held`) and any exit through it; an Enter under way finishes and comes out by a door not held (the service door, else the public door), or waits inside while both are held; a cancelled Enter comes out without Vale by the public door, else the service door, or waits inside while both are held (the wait cannot be cancelled; brief 013 E3). A missed check-in is an empty post, no body: it holds nothing. Counts are kept, not repeated: a later alarm tops them up. One incident is one dispatch (brief 013 D, Aster 2026-10-16): the first landed report of an incident dispatches; a later report of it that raises the Alert tops that dispatch up to the new Alert's counts, from the destinations the first set; any other later report of it sends nothing (a unit already out may be sent on to a scene no unit covers). A robot is a patrol unit (weapons.health.patrol, a pistol, trained) walking at `robotSpeed`; the patrol robot is the first robot when it is on its sweep and answers after `robotWire`; the others and the officers start at the site's docks and posts, else at the response unit's entry; they leave one every `launchGap` ticks. Robots and units stop at `cap` combatants (§06). Destinations, in order, duplicates within witness range dropped: the scene; the missing person's post and the stands his lover, family and workmates are meant to be at now, and his car (up to `spread`); the alarm-raiser's ties likewise (up to `spread`); at Alert 3 the mouths. Robots take them in order, the nearest free robot first, ties on id, each only a place within `robotReach` of where it starts (its dock, or the patrol's place on its sweep): farther places are for officers; units go to the scene, then to the place with the fewest units. A unit within witness range of the scene with a clear line verifies: a body there is confirmed (the act's Trail, a kill's Standing, Alert to the confirmed level; the seal starts only on a confirmation at Alert 2 or more, the level's `seal` after the later of the confirmation and the response unit on the street (the seal is the unit's cordon, as for gunfire; Motive rev 3); a knocked-out victim is brought round and gives his statement); no body is unfounded (Alert stays, no seal). Arriving, a unit checks `check`, then robots hold the point (a watcher) and officers search `search.s`: at Alert 2 or more they open every stash within `search.m` of the scene, nearest first, `search.stash` each; a report from a stash itself (a noise, a round) opens that stash at any Alert. Units stand down `standDown.inquiry` after the last alarm at Alert 1 and `standDown.search` at Alert 2, never at Alert 3. The world places report points and the response's origins by rule, so that every walkable cell is within `world.report` of a report point and within `world.dock` of a dock or post (R-REPORT, R-DOCK, checked by the world's tools; the engine reads the places the world exports). Every staff post checks in by voice every `checkIn` from the start of the shift at the post and at its end: a missed mark is a report that lands at the mark at the post. A person who expects a tie at a stop they share (lover, family, workmate; from the people file's routines, never authored) and is at the place without them, while the tie's routine puts them there and the tie is down, held or stashed, raises the alarm after `suspicion.s` (times `suspicion.pm` by temperament, per mille; default a flat 20 s): a missing-person report from where they stand; a turned waiter says nothing; a person being taken reports nothing.

custody.rule: What a capture at Go leaves the campaign (brief 018 §3), worked at the debrief until a campaign layer runs: +trail per captured operative (the campaign's Trail, so Heat); the operative is held at the district's police post (the non-door post nearest the car) and a rescue is offered there for `missions` missions, after which the operative is moved out of reach (Sky 2026-10-18 answer 2: not lost); wounds carry over. At capture an operative left standing takes resentment +abandonedResentment and loyalty −abandonedLoyalty. Once in each between-missions phase while held: fear +fear, loyalty −loyalty, then the Talker test; every value clamped to its scale; talking is once and for good. The founding cell starts at `cellStart`; recruits keep their own scales. A captive who talks gives cell-face for every operative, cell-car, place-time and contact for every turned contact. The debrief projects it: holds = the missions the captive holds before the questioning it talks at.

campaign.rule: What a takedown leaves the campaign, worked out at the mission's end for the debrief (no campaign layer runs yet). A killing never found in the mission is a missing person: missing.trail (no homicide), no Standing, his family, lover and workmate ties fear +missing.tiesFear (worry), the block where he was last seen gets areaWatch.step posted guard and camera for areaWatch.missions missions, and a case opens that stays open until the body is found. A found killing: takedown.trail.kill with the act's Trail, Standing takedown.foundKillStanding on confirmation, his ties grieve (a turned contact takes the saw-violence move, everyone else fear +missing.tiesFear), the area watch as above, and a case that closes after cases.close missions. A knockout hidden or restrained to the end comes home and gives a statement: the act's Trail and his facts as leads; his own fear +1 (resentment +1 if he saw it coming). The district's security level is its base + floor(open cases / cases.perLevel), at most cases.cap above the base.

rounds.rule: A server who works a terrace (brief 022; the baked round sim/data/handover.rounds.json, made by tools/routines from contracts/people/routines.rules.json, Pulse) walks to the tables on a round clock and back to her post; her position is the round's. The round clock stops while she is held: from the tick an order of a verb in `holds` is taken on her to the tick it lands, plus `linger`; an order taken inside the linger extends the same hold; she stands where she is, turned to the operative. Watch holds nothing. The round ends, for the rest of the mission, at the first of `ends` (Alert 2, any shot, a body found, the final fight): she walks back along her own path and stands her post. Called (the summons): the guard walks to a stop at her side, `close` from her post, facing her: the baked stops (rounds file guard.stops: the ring of `close` round her post, free ground, most lateral first, her left first) are read in order and the first with nobody within `clear` of it at the tick of the call is his (the operatives not down and not inside, the patrol, everyone on the street; not her, not him); if every stop is taken, the stop whose nearest person is farthest, the earlier on a tie; a file with no stop keeps the old stop, `close` short of her post on his own route; she breaks off and walks back to her post, they stand together from his arrival to his turn plus `part`, and her round resumes at the start of its next rest. Summon's reach, its refusals and its walk limit read her post, never her pose.
