target.rule: Every car the mission simulates is a target by its own id (car:getaway, car:official, car:rivals; the range has none; the street's parked and passing cars are the host's dressing, not simulated). A car takes `health` (×fight.lab.healthScale in the lab). At or below `disabledAt` (×healthScale) it is disabled: it stops where it is and never drives again, and its occupants get out on their side and act as people do. At 0 it burns: occupants still able get out at once, and `burn` seconds later it explodes: everyone within `blast.m` with a line to the car takes `blast.damage` (×healthScale), the cell included, and anyone held inside takes it whatever the line. Its cover points are gone once it explodes. Costs, all existing: shooting a car is a shooting (gunfire-trail once, alert.gunfire, the response); the car itself takes no hit or down Trail and no Standing step (property); the blast is violence: seen by a civilian, alert.violenceSeen and a Menace step, once a car; each person it hits is hit by the cell (hit-trail, down-trail, a body if they die), an operative it hits costs no Trail. The getaway car disabled fails the mission getaway-lost (every exit is gone). The official car disabled stays where it stopped and the Take there is still possible; its driver gets out; Vale at the car gets out, and is held inside only while the Enforcer seizes him. The rival car disabled: a broken crew leaves on foot (ai.rivalGone unchanged). Hostiles never choose a car as a target. A fire order on the getaway car, or on the official car with Vale at it, takes the always-hold (GoingLoud.Fails: getaway-lost, vale-dead).

car.drive: Where a car may be (brief 023). The site carries a drive grid (sim/data/handover.site.json `drive`, the walk grid's window and cells, made by tools/sim/drive.ts): a cell is drivable when its centre lies on a carriageway (within half a plan road's width of its centreline), in a kerb bay of the civic block, or on a drive (the world's vehicle crossing from a carriageway over a dropped kerb and the pavement to a bay or yard: civic-block drives[], Splice; the Handover's one is service-drive, Apron Road to serviceBay). Pavements, forecourts, yards and squares are not drivable. Every car that moves on the street routes on drivable cells only, by the walk grid's A* (8 neighbours, no corner cutting, ties by cell index, string-pulled on drivable cells): the official car's move to block the pickup camera and back, and the turned driver's drive to the service bay (by the carriageway and the drive, never across a pavement). A car's place that lies off the drive grid stands at its nearest drivable cell within 6 m (ties: lowest cell); a place with none, or a car's place that no drive reaches from the pickup, rejects the site at load (unknown = reject). A car keeps off the kerb (brief 023, Keel with Pulse): on a carriageway its centre keeps the site's drive.lane (half the city's lane, life.json traffic.laneWidth) from the edge of the drivable ground where it can, on a drive or in a bay it keeps to the middle; the route never runs nearer an edge than its grid cells did (deterministic, sim Grid.CarRoute). Timing is car.pace's: the block move takes the schedule's blockMoveS each way, and the drive to the service bay runs at its surfaces' pace from driverLast, then waits parked in the bay. Parked in the service bay the car faces the site's car.serviceFacing (the bay's long axis, nose away from the drive it came by). The getaway car leaves the street at Go along its exit lane (getaway.exit, held to the carriageway by SX-1); the rival car parks and does not move.
car.paceRule: A moving car drives each drive-grid cell at its surface's pace: `road` on a carriageway, `yard` on a drive or in a bay. The turned driver leaves at driverLast and waits parked in the service bay until Vale comes; the block move keeps the schedule's blockMoveS (a manoeuvre out of the bay, not a drive).

The final fight moves Standing once when it ends (fight.public) and adds no Trail or Alert (traced). Fire orders on anyone else are untouched.

kite.rule: Armed hostiles shot at from beyond their reach answer (brief 027 F2, Pulse briefs/027/pulse/kite-response.md with the retest fixes; promoted to today by Sky 2026-10-20, tuning.md §7.9; the lab keeps it on, fight.lab.kite). An operative's shot that lands on an armed hostile marks every living body of the target's side (police: the response unit and the final-fight officers; the brief-013 police units of its dispatch, never robots; rivals: the ambush crew; the pre-fight crew on its own) with the shooter. `react` after the first shot, a body no operative with a weapon out stands inside its effective ring of acts: police close in to the first point of the grid route to the shooter within ai.stopReach of their effective ring, re-planned every `replan`, at most `chase` of walk counted within `contact` of the shooter (a capped body re-arms after `rearm` while the shooter still fires), then hold the cover that shields them within ai.seek.police; a police unit at its scene answers off its post. Police shot at within weapons.lineLapse (3 s), hit or miss, by an operative they have a line to fire back while that shooter is inside their weapon's max ring (every operative who fired on them in that window, not only the last: tuning.md §12.2, engine 0.17.0; the cover below only when they can answer none of them), from where they stand, keeping their cover, at their band's odds (Motive tuning.md §7.10 rule 1; final-fight officers, the response unit, the police units; never robots, the door guard or the patrol). In the final fight, a police body shot from out of its reach takes the cover that shields it, fires back to its max ring, and after `coverHold` with the shooter still out of its max, closes to the shielding cover nearest its stop point of the shooter (within ai.seek.police of it; none: the stop point itself), at a walk, firing as it walks at weapons.mod for its gait (tuning.md §8.3, Sky 2026-10-21; was: nothing while it walks), and plans again each `coverHold` while shots land; unshielded, it plans again `react` after its last plan. It never chases a runner: only a shooter who has fired within `lapse` keeps the alarm. The blocker keeps its lane and answers by the max-ring rule only (§7.10 rule 4, as §7.11.1 narrowed it: the lab's contest officer answers as any police body does). Rivals step out of the line (cover that shields them, else a blind point within 8 m); the pre-fight crew walks out, holds, and walks back `hide` after the last shot on it (its arrival late by the detour), advances to its effective ring of the shooter with no hide, and advances after `hideMax` held. `lapse` with no shot on its side clears the alarm.

lab.rule: EXPERIMENTAL (brief 027 playground; briefs/027/playground.md §2, §3). With the lab on: every health is weapons.health × healthScale; the cell carries the loadout (each weapon's arms within the mission's Arms; the carbine is the cell's), every other gun the lab sidearm; a hit does the weapon's damage (the riot gun nearDamage within near). With pips on, a shot's chance is a step of `chance`: the range band (4 within weapons.pointBlank, 3 within the weapon's eff, 2 within its max), then −1 an untrained shooter and −1 a target still beside cover that shields it (both beyond point blank), −1 a walking shooter, +1 a shooter on a higher level than the target, clamped 1–4; a shooter running toward or across −`runPips` (floor 0), a shooter running away 0 pips whatever the band (tuning.md §8.3); 0 pips is the `pip0` step; a target running this tick past point blank takes weapons.mod.targetRunning on the step's chance; counted by the accumulator (weapons.mod.vale is not read). Aim memory (tuning.md §6.1–6.2; today has it too since §13.1, from acc.start): the count is the pair (shooter, target)'s, for the whole mission and for every shooter (cell, rivals, police, response units): taking a target resumes the count the shooter left on it, and nothing resets it (cease, hold, holster, the draw, an order's end, a volley's end, a walk into range, a switch); a target the shooter has not fired at starts at accStart (today's acc.start is not read). Any switch still waits aimNew (the next shot no sooner than aimNew after taking the target). Off: today's multipliers. Drawing takes `draw`, a new target `aimNew`. Stances `three` (tuning.md §13.4, engine 0.18.0): today's hold, return and free, and a draw sets return. Stances `two` (an option): drawn fires at will (free) or holds (hold); return is refused; a fire order clears hold. `then` free: a fire order whose target is down returns the agent to at will. `close`: a fire order out of range or with no line walks the grid to the nearest free point inside the weapon's effective ring with a clear line (nearest by walk, ties by cell), then fires; it neither lapses nor is refused for range (a driven agent is never walked). Charge (on): each agent holds up to max; a weapon with a charge pays it each shot and does not fire short of it; charge comes back regen a tick once the agent has rested charge.rest since its last charged shot or targeted shot (a volley's shot, any weapon, stamps it; a refund stamps nothing; tuning.md §6.3). A volley {op, target, shots} fires exactly `shots` (1..target.maxShots) at the target at the weapon's cadence, then the agent returns to its stance; it pays the weapon's target charge a shot when given (with charge off: one of target.volleysPerFight a fight), refused no-charge if unpaid, and gets back what it did not fire when it ends early. The field (on): {do: field} pays field.cost, absorbs up to field.absorb damage for field.ticks, and the agent fires nothing while it holds. Police warning (on): an officer, guard, patrol or response unit who sees a drawn weapon before any shot of the run gives policeWarning.ticks to holster: holstered in time, Alert policeWarning.alert, the face is remembered and the watcher logs it (+policeWarning.trail Trail once a shout), no engagement; still drawn, today's drawn-seen (Alert to weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity, he engages and calls it in). Each watcher shouts at most policeWarning.perWatcher times a mission (tuning.md §6.4): an agent he sees drawn while his shout is open joins it (the same window); once it has closed, the next drawn weapon he sees before any shot is drawn-seen at once. Cameras and rivals never warn. hostilesFireMoving: a final-fight hostile stepping to cover or walking its lane fires as it walks (−1 pip; today's moving modifier with pips off). Panic is allowed outside a fight. kite (on; brief 027 F2, Pulse briefs/027/pulse/kite-response.md; Motive tuning.md §6.6): an operative's shot that lands (hit or miss) on an armed hostile alarms every living body of its side with the shooter (police: the response unit, joined or not, and the final-fight officers; rivals: the ambush crew; the pre-fight crew is its own side; police units: the brief-013 police-n of one dispatch; never the guard, the patrol, civilians or robots). kite.react after the first shot a body acts unless it sees an operative with a weapon out inside its effective ring (by its own sight; it keeps its own fight). Police walk the grid route toward the shooter to the first point within ai.stopReach of their effective ring, re-planned every kite.replan, at most kite.chase of walk a body a run (then the cover that shields it from the shooter within ai.seek.police, held); a holder does not walk home while its alarm is open. The ambush crew takes the cover that shields it from the shooter within ai.seek.rival (once each cover.stepGap), else the nearest free point within 8 m with no line to the shooter; the pre-fight crew walks out to that point, holds, and walks back once kite.hide passes with no shot on it, its arrival clock later by the detour; with no such point it stands. kite.lapse with no shot on its side clears a body's alarm. Retest (brief 027; Suture retest.md R1–R4, Pulse retest-fixes.md, Motive tuning.md §7.2–7.5): the chase budget counts only the walk the answer itself orders while the body is within kite.contact of the shooter (a body's own walk, the walk in, its advance and a blocker's lane never count); a remainder shorter than a grid cell is spent; a spent budget, the alarm still open, re-arms after kite.rearm. A police unit at its scene (check, search, hold) answers as the response unit does, off its post until it walks on. In the final fight no police body chases: shot by an operative it cannot answer, it takes the cover that shields it from him within ai.seek.police and no farther from the car than its stand, and that point becomes its stand; with no such cover it closes to the first point of its route to him within ai.stopReach of its effective ring (keeping the cover it held), and that point becomes its stand (a police unit walks there off its post; Suture retest2.md N1, N4; Pulse reviews the motion). It plans again once where it stands no longer shields it from where he stands now, no sooner than kite.react after its last plan (a shielded body holds; Suture retest3.md N7). The blocker keeps its lane. The pre-fight crew with no hide advances to its effective ring of the shooter (the ambush crew too); out of the line it walks on toward a shooter in its band (beyond its effective ring, within its max) who still fires, once each kite.replan, and leans back out only once no operative with a weapon out stands within its max ring of the lean-out point on a line, else after kite.hideMax it walks on toward him; its advances spend its chase budget. policeContest: in a loud final fight the first n officers take as their stand the first point of the route from their stand to the getaway car within ai.stopReach of their effective ring of it. With the lab on, the pre-fight crew driven back has its hit flag cleared with its health (each drive-back's first hit is +hit-trail), and a shot landing later in that tick finds it gone. A move never snaps onto a cover point a hostile stands on or walks to. coverSnap (on, B5): a drawn operative's move order to a point on the ground (walk or run; never a move to a named place, a mission point or a person's) whose end lies within coverSnap.snap of a cover point of the site (contracts/world/civic-block.cover.json, present at the mission second, quality at least ai.cover.qPartial) that is free (held by no other body: a hostile that took it or another operative that snapped to it) and joined to the end by a straight walkable line (never through a wall or the cover object) ends on that point instead: the one that shields against the nearest combatant first, then the nearest, then the lower id. The operative holds the point while it walks to it or stands within ai.cover.snap of it; down, inside, in the car or moved off, it lets it go. The shield is still ai.cover's (standing still, inside the point's arc, beyond point blank: −1 pip). A walk into range (close) and a driven agent never snap (stepping out of the car is a move, and does). A holstered operative's move never snaps (a walk on a route stays where it was clicked). fight.rule: The final fight (§07 [S]: always; up to 60 s, Sky 2026-10-18; 3–5 hostiles) starts when the Enforcer has Vale. Loud (any shot or Alert ≥ 2): police officers run in from the response unit's entry, base `loud.officers`, +`loud.alert` if Alert reached 3, +`loud.civilian` if a civilian was shot; the seal clock runs; no allies. Safe (no shots, Alert ≤ 1): the rival crew ambushes the extraction when the Enforcer brings Vale within `safe.ambush` of the getaway car: `safe.hostiles`, −`safe.minus` if the driver is turned (he blocks the rival car), −`safe.minus` if the rivals were tipped off earlier; a helped Inez warns `safe.warn` early (the first volley comes that much later); the guard, if he never saw the cell and was never shot, runs in and fights them (he fires as a guard does). Every hostile drops at `cell.fire.hits` hits. Each hostile fires at its own weapon's cadence (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: the volley is retired). The hold (brief 018, Sky 2026-10-18): the car can't leave while a holder stands: a combatant not down, broken or gone within `hold` of the car (any level, line or none) or on the street inside the exit lane, the first `block` of the getaway route's carriageway ahead of the car at the road's width (site getaway.exit, derived from the plan by tools/sim/getaway.ts). An ambusher lying in wait holds only if its spot does. The blocker: `blockers` hostiles per fight go for the road, the one with the shortest grid walk to the lane (safe: an ambusher, moving when the ambush springs; loud: the first officer to arrive, instead of a police stop; ties by id), scored by the grid walk to the post it would take (brief 018 §10, Pulse): the nearest free cover point inside the lane between `blockNear` and `blockFar` of the car point (straight line, as the hold), else the open lane centreline `blockNear` along the lane from its start; it walks there without stopping and holds it as police hold a stand; downed, broken or gone it is not replaced, and a rival blocker breaks with its crew. A rival within `cell.atReach` of the car while Vale is in it, with no operative standing within `cell.reach` of the car, reaches Vale (rivals-reach-vale). The Enforcer down fails the mission only while Vale is not yet in the car. Seen leaving (cell.rule): a final-fight officer sees the car go if it has a clear line to it within weapons.pistol.max.

investigation.rule: Between the mission and its debrief the city works the Trail (§05 output: findings → debrief Investigation state → next mission). If campaign Trail is at least trail-open, base + perAlert × the mission's Alert investigators each follow `hops` leads. A lead is an incident (an act seen, a shooting, a report: its place, time and witnesses) or a watcher's sighting (§05 watchers: place + time); the newest unfollowed lead goes first. At a lead they question the simulated people who saw it (Sky Q5), nearest first, then by id, one person a hop, each at most once, through investigator.question: a Talker gives every fact they hold and each fact's place-time becomes a lead; a liar gives what people.rules talker.lie says; anyone else, or anyone holding nothing, gives nothing and the hop is spent (K6). drift-standing moves the district at most `step` toward `to`, never past it: nothing at the start
both outcomes write the district's one Standing line (debrief.lines.standing) with its cause from standing.causes
events.reason: Motive: what the city stops seeing, it forgives; symmetric, so unkept Hero fades back to +2 as Menace does. Last in the phase (Motive had it after standing.word) so that a killing found between missions counts as a move.
